title: Skill curriculum - authority-free training and evaluation material for canonical skills
description: A curriculum is what a skill teaches and how a run against it is judged. It is compiled from a canonical skill manifest and never replaces it: the manifest keeps the permissions, the router keeps the routing, the Model Mesh keeps the model. A curriculum entry that widened any of those would be describing a skill that does not exist.

source_of_truth.description: Where the material is compiled from. Recorded so a curriculum can be regenerated rather than edited into divergence from the skill it describes.

authority.description: Denied by name rather than by omission. A file that never mentions routing does not tell a reader whether it routes.

role_id.description: A role branch id. Matched by shape, not by an enumerated copy: the canonical list lives in AI_SKILL_LIBRARY/v4/model_mesh/role_branches.yaml and a second copy here would be a second vocabulary to keep in sync.

eval.description: A frozen, replayable unit. suite_hash binds a score to the exact suite that produced it, so a reworded suite cannot inherit an old result.

permissions.description: Inherited from the skill manifest verbatim. The ceiling is the manifest's; compilation may narrow the description of it but never widen what it permits.

privacy_constraints.description: Required, not optional. Section 4.1 of the design lists privacy constraints among the things a curriculum contains, and section 8 requires the compiler to preserve the original skill's privacy restrictions. An entry that simply omits the field is indistinguishable from one compiled off a skill that had no restrictions to preserve, and the compiler would have no way to tell that it had dropped them.

protected_invariants.description: Required, not optional. Tolerance on the protected dimensions of section 12 is zero, and an entry that never names what it must not break cannot be checked for having broken it.

allOf.description: Section 11: learning must never lower a risk class. The classes run from A (may auto-promote through the existing evidence gates) to D (never auto-promotes), so a promotion_class earlier in that order than the entry's own risk_class hands a class-D authority, security or trading change the auto-promotion path of a class-A wording tweak. Expressed as a constraint because the alternative is trusting that no compiler ever emits the pair, and the pair validated cleanly before this.
allOf.$comment: One branch per risk class above A; risk_class A already admits every promotion_class.

allOf.description: risk_class B admits only promotion_class B or C or D.
risk_class C admits only promotion_class C or D.
risk_class D admits only promotion_class D.
